title: The Key to Reading Micro Expressions
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article frames micro expressions, brief, involuntary facial expressions lasting a fraction of a second, as the most direct window into what people are actually feeling, even when they're trying to conceal it. It notes research showing 15 emotions are expressed through the same facial patterns universally across cultures, from disgust to pride to shame. The recommended training method is practicing expressions deliberately in a mirror, closely observing the exact facial changes each emotion produces, which sharpens a leader's ability to detect the same expressions fleetingly in others. The piece closes with a research-based caution: facial expressions don't just reveal emotion, they can also generate it, so practicing happiness on purpose can genuinely make a leader feel happier.
points: Micro expressions are brief, involuntary facial signals that reveal true emotion even when someone is actively trying to hide it.
Research shows 15 emotions produce the same facial expressions universally across cultures, from the U.S. to Singapore to New Guinea.
Practicing expressions deliberately in a mirror is the recommended training method for sharpening the ability to detect fleeting expressions in others.
Facial expressions don't just reveal emotion, research shows they can also generate it, meaning practicing positive expressions can shift a leader's actual mood.
